title: Cross-browser anchor & snap behaviors for console panels, modals, and charts
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Design and prototype a robust set of anchor and 'snap' behaviors for the Redwood Console to ensure predictable layout and interaction across browsers and viewport sizes. This ticket covers three surface families: left/right docking panels and splitters, modal dialogs and action drawers, and chart/canvas surfaces that need sticky anchors and overflow fallthrough. Goal: eliminate janky reflows, ensure keyboard focus continuity, and provide graceful fallbacks on legacy browsers (Safari 14, IE Edge compat mode) and constrained devices.
background: Several customer support threads and recent Playbook sessions reported inconsistent modal stacking and chart clipping on Safari iOS and older MacOS Chrome versions. Engineering reported flaky scroll lock behavior when autoscaling panels during bursty cost-explorer loads. This work aims to standardize patterns, document CSS/JS fallbacks, and hand a testable Figma prototype and engineering spec to frontend teams.
out_of_scope: Full refactor of the grid system or virtualization engine; replacing charting library. Performance micro-optimizations will be tracked in follow-up ENG tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Panels (left/right) maintain anchor position when viewport height changes; no content overlap with headers or global banners.
Modals support three fallthrough states: centered, anchored-bottom (mobile), and fullscreen (narrow width) with consistent focus trapping and ARIA roles.
Charts with pinned legends support sticky anchoring without causing horizontal scroll jitter at common breakpoints (>=320px <=1920px).
All behaviors verified on Chrome, Firefox, Safari (desktop & iOS), and Edge; documented graceful degradations for unsupported features.
Design tokens and CSS utility classes provided for engineering with examples and a small JS polyfill for intersection/resize edge cases.
Hand-off includes Figma prototype, interaction spec, and a short test matrix used during engineering review.

test_matrix: Desktop Firefox 110+ (macOS/Win): pass with minor repaint differences
Desktop Safari 15+ (macOS): polyfill required for sticky -> tested
Mobile Safari iOS 14-17: anchored-bottom modal layout adjustment and handle affordance required
Legacy mode (IE Edge compatibility): graceful fallback - modals collapse to fullscreen
user_research_summary: Five quick usability sessions with product teams and two external customers: consistent preference for anchored modals on narrow widths; confusion when focus order jumped due to unexpected stacking. Recommended clear visual handles and animation easing to communicate state transitions.
handoff_items: CSS utility token list (z-index, spacing, sticky-thresholds)
Small JS polyfill module with tests
QA test matrix and repro steps
notes: Prefer CSS-first approach; polyfill only where not feasible. Keep animations subtle to avoid layout thrashing. Coordinate rollout with cost-explorer A/B canary.
